title: George Lewis and Willie Humphrey in the 1920s
summary: George Lewis's rise around 1922, the after-hours jam spot, his unchanged style, and Willie Humphrey following.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, George started coming in the eye of the public around, I'd say around 22. Mm-hmm. In 1922. Because we was playing at, uh, at, uh, Humming Booth, at, uh, Elite. And when we'd get through there, I had a place back, Iberville Street, that, Iberville and Mariette called, uh, the Boothwa. Uh, all the musicians used to go back there when they get off on wake. All of them used to go back there to jam. Jam that is six, seven o'clock the next morning. Well, George was playing a lot of clarinet then. So I'd say he was about to next around here.
And was his style similar to his today or different?
No, just about the same as it is today.

Now I could tell him anywhere he had. Same style he played on. And then, uh, Willie Humphrey stepped in the picture then. Because he's a little clarinet player than either one of us. But he stepped in the picture after, uh, George began to travel.
And then Willie Humphrey come out.
